messages.content: What is the best month to visit Hawaii?

message.content:
The “best” month to visit Hawaii depends on what you’re looking for, but most travelers agree that the shoulder seasons—**April, May, September, and October**—offer the best balance of pleasant weather, lower crowds, and more reasonable prices.

| Month | Why it’s great |
|-------|----------------|
| **April** | Warm temperatures (mid‑70s °F / 24–26 °C), lower hotel rates, and fewer tourists after the spring break rush. |
| **May** | Similar warmth, even fewer crowds, and the start of the summer surf season. |
| **September** | Post‑summer lull, still warm (mid‑70s °F), and the start of the fall season when many locals return home. |
| **October** | Mild temperatures (low‑70s °F), fewer visitors, and the beginning of the winter trade wind season. |

### Quick comparison of average temperatures (Hawaii – Honolulu)

| Month | Avg. High | Avg. Low |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| April | 81 °F (27 °C) | 66 °F (19 °C) |
| May | 83 °F (28 °C) | 68 °F (20 °C) |
| September | 84 °F (29 °C) | 69 °F (21 °C) |
| October | 82 °F (28 °C) | 67 °F (19 °C) |

These months give you warm, sunny days without the peak‑season crowds or the higher prices of July and August. If you’re a surfer, you might prefer the summer months for stronger swells, but for a relaxed vacation with good deals, April, May, September, or October are your best bets.
